_desc: Head-to-head MADDPG offloading baseline (following Zhong et al. IoT-J 2026 learner) vs LyaMAPPO. Fair-footing: same env / DVFS substrate / completion incentive as all learned baselines; DoD-aware (use_dod_penalty) but NO HL half-life term (use_battery_loss=False, W_HL=0), faithful to the paper which optimizes DoD not HL. n=5 eval seeds, T_EVAL=5400, lambda_high=4.0. Best checkpoint by max-CR, step 2000.

MADDPG_DoD.footing: fair (env reward + completion incentive, 54-dim actor, 245-dim centralized critic, shared DVFS); MADDPG learner (Gumbel-Softmax + centralized critic); no battery virtual queue / no task-level advantage decomposition

_takeaways: Fair-footing MADDPG is competitive on service: satisfaction 0.836 (even edges LyaMAPPO 0.788), delay 3.00s, queue 2.4 -- a credible strong baseline, not a strawman.
But it incurs ~3x worse battery health: cumHL 2.795 vs LyaMAPPO 0.952 (HL/slot 5.18 vs 1.76 e-4).
Lacking LyaMAPPO's battery virtual queue z_n and task-level advantage decomposition, MADDPG trades battery lifetime for throughput -- LyaMAPPO Pareto-dominates on the battery-lifetime moat.
This places MADDPG in the high-throughput/high-HL cluster (with TD3-Sched 0.837/2.39, MHSPO 0.799/2.75, MAPPO_NoBat 0.822/2.87), all beaten by LyaMAPPO's uniquely low cumHL 0.952.
